concepts.name: Graphs of functions
concepts.about: y = f(x), drawn on graph paper.

concepts.name: Trigonometry
concepts.about: Sine and cosine turn an angle into a position.

concepts.name: Polar curves
concepts.about: A distance r that depends on the angle.

concepts.name: Parametric curves
concepts.about: x and y each a function of a third variable, t.

concepts.name: Spirals
concepts.about: Curves that wind outward as they turn.

concepts.name: Fractions
concepts.about: Parts of a whole: here, slices of a full turn.

concepts.name: Polygons and stars
concepts.about: Straight sides and the turns between them.

concepts.name: Symmetry and rotation
concepts.about: Shapes that look the same turned or reflected.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.about: Counting that wraps around, like a clock.

concepts.name: Recursion
concepts.about: A drawing defined by smaller copies of itself.

concepts.name: L-systems
concepts.about: A word rewritten by rules, then read as turtle moves.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.about: Points of the plane that multiply: z² + c, again and again.

concepts.name: Linear algebra
concepts.about: Vectors and matrices: combining arrows, and stretching and turning the plane.

examples.name: Sine waves
examples.about: y = a sin(bx): amplitude stretches the wave, frequency squeezes it.

examples.name: Parabolas
examples.about: y = ax², narrower as a grows, and a shifted vertex.

examples.name: Damped oscillation
examples.about: A swing that shrinks inside its exponential envelope.

examples.name: Square wave from sines
examples.about: A Fourier series: odd harmonics add up to a square wave.

examples.name: Rose curve
examples.about: r = cos(7θ/4): petals that close after four turns.

examples.name: Maurer rose
examples.about: Jumping around a rose 71 degrees at a time.

examples.name: Times tables on a circle
examples.about: Join i to 2i mod 200 and a cardioid appears.

examples.name: Lissajous figure
examples.about: Two pendulum swings, 3 to 4, traced together.

examples.name: Spirograph
examples.about: A wheel rolling inside a ring: a hypotrochoid.

examples.name: Butterfly curve
examples.about: Temple Fay's polar curve, twelve turns before it repeats.

examples.name: Archimedean spiral
examples.about: r = aθ: every turn the same distance apart.

examples.name: Sunflower seeds
examples.about: Seeds placed by the golden angle pack without gaps.

examples.name: Fibonacci spiral
examples.about: Quarter circles in squares of side 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, …

examples.name: Squiral
examples.about: Longer steps and 89° turns twist a square spiral.

examples.name: Koch snowflake
examples.about: An endless outline around a finite area.

examples.name: Sierpinski triangle
examples.about: Three half-size copies of itself, all the way down.

examples.name: Fractal tree
examples.about: Every branch is a smaller tree.

examples.name: Dragon curve
examples.about: A strip of paper folded in half eleven times.

examples.name: Equivalent fractions
examples.about: 1/2, 2/4, 3/6 and 4/8 of a pie: the same half, cut finer.

examples.name: Halves forever
examples.about: 1/2 + 1/4 + 1/8 + … fills the circle; 1/4 + 1/16 + … fills a third.

examples.name: Petals from arcs
examples.about: Two arcs of 1/12, 1/6 or 1/4 of a circle make a petal.

examples.name: Yin and yang
examples.about: Three half circles cut a circle into two equal halves.

examples.name: Hilbert curve
examples.about: One line through every cell of a grid, never crossing itself.

examples.name: L-system plant
examples.about: Two rewriting rules and a stack grow a branching plant.

examples.name: Gosper curve
examples.about: An L-system whose curve fills a snowflake-shaped island.

examples.name: Mandelbrot set
examples.about: The points c where z² + c, from 0, never runs away.

examples.name: Julia set
examples.about: Fix c = -0.8 + 0.156i and ask which starting points stay.

examples.name: Star polygons
examples.about: {n/k}: join every k-th of n points on a circle.

examples.name: Rosette
examples.about: One circle drawn 36 times, 10° apart.

examples.name: Linear combinations
examples.about: Two steps of one column and three of another reach b: the column picture of a system.

examples.name: A linear map on a grid
examples.about: A matrix turns the square grid into a slanted one; the unit square's area becomes the determinant.

examples.name: Eigenvectors
examples.about: Most vectors turn when a matrix moves them; eigenvectors only stretch.

examples.name: Least squares
examples.about: The line through scattered points whose squared misses add up to the least.

examples.name: Singular value decomposition
examples.about: Any matrix turns the unit circle into an ellipse, along perpendicular axes.
